newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC to scrutinize News Corp-PrimeStar deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC to scrutinize News Corp-PrimeStar deal.

text.p: The decision by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd to team up with PrimeStar Partners to offer satellite television will get "close scrutiny" from the Federal Communications Commission, an FCC official said Wednesday.
"It is a major development in the market," Peter Cowhey, head of the FCC's international bureau, told Reuters. "It will get close scrutiny."

PrimeStar, a satellite-dish TV service owned by the biggest U.S. cable operators, said it would restructure into a public company that will include U.S. satellite assets from News Corp and MCI Communications Corp.
Cowhey said the FCC "will want to know how this is going to affect the market for multi-channel video services."
He listed several areas in which the agency will be interested:
-- How the deal would affect control of channel capacity on satellites used to beam TV programs around the nation.
-- The impact on the three oribtal satellite slots now capable of beaming programs nationwide. News Corp and MCI will contribute one of the three slots.
A unit of one of PrimeStar's current partners, Tele-Communications Inc, now shares one of the two other orbital slots with EchoStar Communications Corp.
New Corp's chief lobbyist, Peggy Binzel, said PrimeStar has agreed to sell the rights to the 11 transponders on that slot and occupy only the 28 transponders on the MCI slot.
-- The impact on competition between providers of traditional cable TV, high-powered direct-broadcast satellite (DBS) TV, and direct-to-home (DTH) satellite TV.
DBS susbscribers are able to receive signals on a smaller dish than DTH subscribers.
